minutes.headline: Personnel Committee leaned toward dropping step one and moving to 3% between steps, and asked for costed FY25 grids by March 11.
minutes.summary: The committee worked through six FY24 salary-grid scenarios prepared by the town accountant and debated how to align the non-union salary grid with the clerical union. It narrowed to three scenarios to cost out, agreed to drop grade one so grades run two through seventeen, and asked for FY25 grids at 3% on top. Meetings were set for March 11 and tentatively March 13 to reach a recommendation before the warrant article goes to the Select Board and Finance Committee.

attendees.role: referenced official (prepared the grids; mentioned as returning)

votes.motion: Adjourn at 6:29 p.m. (motion and second made)

budget_items.topic: FY24 shift-one scenario (everyone moves up one grade)
budget_items.what_was_said: Nancy gave a total cost for moving every employee one grade up at about 2.54% between steps. Members questioned bumping everyone into new grades with no validation.

budget_items.topic: Scenario drop step one, 3% between steps, no grade change
budget_items.what_was_said: Removes step one and adds a step at the end, with employees staying in their grade. Cost was similar to the first option.

budget_items.topic: Scenario one: adjust grade one to minimum wage
budget_items.what_was_said: Adjusts step one to minimum wage with 2.54% between steps, employees stay put. Cost was roughly half the others.

budget_items.topic: Scenario two: grid starts at minimum wage with lower step increments
budget_items.what_was_said: Grid starts at a higher minimum wage with a smaller percentage between steps and employees keep grade and step.

budget_items.topic: Scenarios three and four: salary survey-based step one
budget_items.what_was_said: Scenario three uses the survey minimum average as step one at 3% between steps; scenario four estimates a reasonable step one per grade. Members doubted how the figures were derived.

budget_items.topic: Scenarios five and six: regrade or eliminate grades one through three
budget_items.what_was_said: Regrading the bottom grades into grade four, or dropping grades one to three, was costed but members said it would not work because of the library page and assistant gap.

budget_items.topic: Cost of preferred drop-step-one option versus budgeted increase
budget_items.what_was_said: Members noted the preferred option is high at the stated figure since the grid was already raised last year, but it matches the clerical 3%.
A member compared the clerical group's cost for 17 people with this group's cost for 85 people, arguing fairness and equity.
The committee compared the administrative assistant ranges in the grid against the clerical union FY24 range.

budget_items.topic: Using existing salary-line surplus to cover retro
budget_items.what_was_said: Members asked whether surplus in the salary line from vacancies could cover retroactive pay without a line item transfer. Others noted consultant costs and higher-step hires might eliminate any cushion.
The committee noted the grade-two step-one rate is already above state minimum wage and further state increases have historically been small.

budget_items.topic: Clerical FY25 range for administrative assistant
budget_items.what_was_said: The FY25 clerical range was reported, implying a modest rise at the top, and the committee noted it would be slightly ahead.
The committee would apply 3% on top of each FY24 scenario for FY25, based loosely on clerical rates and market. Any article would go to town meeting.

transfers.description: Discussed whether unspent salary-line money could cover the retro without a line-item transfer; no transfer was made.

decisions.decision: The committee asked that three scenarios be costed: drop step one with 3% between steps; scenario one with grade one dropped and 3% between steps; and scenario two with 3% between steps instead of 2.2.
Agreement to drop grade one and run the grid as grades two through seventeen, keeping 16 grades.
For the next meeting, the three new FY24 scenarios will be laid out, and FY25 grids will be prepared by adding 3% on top of each.
A separate discussion will be held on which individual jobs should be reclassified to a higher grade, apart from the grid change.
Next meetings set for Monday March 11 at 5:00 pm, with Wednesday March 13 tentatively held in case more time is needed.
The grid and retro numbers must be ready so the warrant article can go to the Select Board and Finance Committee ahead of book printing.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee asked for three salary-grid scenarios to be costed, including dropping step one with 3% between steps.
The committee agreed to drop grade one and run the non-union grid as grades two through seventeen, keeping 16 grades.
FY25 grids will be prepared by adding 3% on top of each of the three new FY24 scenarios for the next meeting.
Members compared the clerical union's cost for 17 people with this group's cost for 85 people, citing fairness between the two groups.
Meetings were set for March 11 at 5:00 pm, with March 13 held tentatively, so the grid and retro figures can reach the warrant article.

why_it_matters: The non-union salary grid sets pay for about 85 town employees, and any scenario chosen adds a cost to the town's FY24 and FY25 budgets and may come to a Town Meeting vote as a warrant article.
The retroactive pay raises the question of whether vacancy savings in the salary line can cover it or whether a line-item transfer would be needed.

The warrant article on the grid and retro pay going to the Select Board and Finance Committee ahead of book printing.
